findings.description: `pup usage --json` prints worker-writable model, effort and tool names with DEL and C1 controls (such as U+009B CSI) still raw, because `JSON.stringify` only escapes U+0000–U+001F; the ADR says `--json` "escapes them already".
findings.body:
**Concern.** ADR 0122 *Print* says the model, effort and tool names come from a file a worker can write. The text report scrubs each one with `sanitizeReason` (decision 68), and the ADR claims "`--json` escapes them already". That claim is only half true:

- `JSON.stringify` escapes U+0000–U+001F, `"` and `\`.
- It leaves DEL (U+007F) and the C1 range U+0080–U+009F as raw characters.
- `sanitizeReason` deliberately strips `[\u007f-\u009f]` (`src/adapters/capability.utils.ts:78`). The PR's own test plants `'hi\u009bgh'` as an effort to check exactly this, but only on the text path.

Nothing upstream sanitizes these values: `parseCall` copies `entry.message?.model` and `entry.effort` raw, `noteAssistant` stores the raw `block.name`, and `sanitizeReason` is only called inside `formatUsageReport`.

**Exploit path.** A worker plants a line such as `{"type":"assistant","requestId":"r","timestamp":"…","effort":"x\u009b2J…","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","usage":{}}}` in a `.jsonl` file in its own transcript directory. `workerDirsOf` adds that directory. When the operator runs `pup usage --json`, U+009B reaches their terminal as the UTF-8 bytes `C2 9B`. Terminals that treat UTF-8-encoded C1 as control (xterm by default, VTE) read it as CSI. That gives the same screen and title rewriting decision 68 closes for every other print site. Whether a terminal acts on C1 varies by terminal, hence medium confidence.

```ts
console.log(opts.json ? JSON.stringify(report, null, 2) : formatUsageReport(report));
```

<https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/fe05149ec1cb3a36f7fe97268fe8111e42d43fc2/src/cli/index.ts#L2514>
ADR claim: <https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/fe05149ec1cb3a36f7fe97268fe8111e42d43fc2/docs/adr/0122-pup-usage-reports-where-the-claude-usage-went-from-the.md#L37-L45>

The fix below loses nothing. In `JSON.stringify` output, a non-ASCII character can only appear inside a string literal, so writing it as `\uXXXX` is still valid JSON and parses back to the same value. A `--json` test that plants `\u009b` would pin the fix.

findings.description: `new Set(opts.claudeDirs ...)` dedupes the config dirs by raw string. If `--session-env` does not name `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` and the shell sets it to the default dir in another spelling (e.g. `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=$HOME/.claude/` with a trailing slash), `claudeDirs` holds `~/.claude` twice. Every transcript is then scanned twice, and calls and cost come out doubled with no sign of it. Resolving each dir before deduping fixes the trailing-slash and relative-path cases (needs `resolve` from `node:path`).

The utility class only exists for transcripts in the checkout's own directory. `classOf` returns `source.class` unchanged for any file found in a worktree directory. The decision-record `claude -p` (utility.service.ts:21, called from merge-gate.service.ts:2227) runs with no `cwd`, so it writes its transcript under whatever directory `pup merge` was run from. Run from inside a worktree, that headless Haiku call is counted as `worker`. Run from a subdirectory such as `/repo/src`, it is missed entirely. Applying the `headless -> Utility` check before the source-class shortcut fixes the first case.

The test 'reads the transcripts of the config dir --session-env names' cannot tell whether `claudeUserDir` / `--session-env` is used at all. It stubs `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=configDir`, so the second `claudeDirs` entry (`process.env.CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR ?? ~/.claude`) is already `configDir`. The test still passes if you drop `saveSessionEnv(repo, ['CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR'])`, or drop `userDir` from `claudeDirs` (index.ts:2512). To pin the windows' dir, the test needs a case where the two entries differ.

`pup usage` works out the operator shell's config dir in the CLI layer (`process.env.CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR ?? join(homedir(), '.claude')`). That copies a decision `src/claude/` already makes in `claudeUserDir`/`namedConfigDir` (session-runtime.service.ts:394-433). It also adds a third place that hard-codes `~/.claude`, next to `claudeUserDir` and the `transcriptDir` default. And it pulls `homedir` into a CLI that is meant to stay thin. This is Duplicated Code plus Claude-specific logic leaking out of the only module allowed to own it. A small exported helper in session-runtime.service.ts (for example `shellClaudeDir()`) next to `claudeUserDir` would keep both answers in one place.

`UsageOptions.claudeDirs` is optional and falls back to `[join(homedir(), '.claude')]`. No caller uses the fallback: the CLI (index.ts:2513) and both test call sites (usage-report.test.ts:89, :217) always pass `claudeDirs`. This is Speculative Generality. The fallback is the only reason the service imports `homedir`, and it repeats the `~/.claude` default that `src/claude/` owns. Making the field required removes the branch and the import.

The seven-day default for `--since` is written inline as `7 * 86_400_000`, against general.md §No hardcoded values ("none are inlined at the use site"). `DAY_MS` is already exported from `src/core/web-dashboard-sheet.utils.ts:24`. Name the default in a constants file and reuse `DAY_MS`.

The boolean fields `conductor`, `headless` (in `ReadTranscript` and `ScanState`) and `sawUser` (in `ScanState`) break the general.md rule that boolean names start with `is`/`has`/`should`/`can`. Rename them to `isConductor`, `isHeadless` and `hasSeenUser`.

The `subagentFiles` JSDoc says it returns "Every `<session>/subagents/agent-*.jsonl`". `jsonlIn` only filters on the `.jsonl` extension, so the code takes any `.jsonl` in that folder and the `agent-*` part of the doc overstates what it matches.

The ADR's `*Tests.*` paragraph lists the fixtures and CLI refusal cases the tests cover. It will go stale as the tests change, and it already misses the relative-`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` refusal and the `--session-env` config-dir case in `src/cli/index.test.ts`. Consider deleting it.
